clue.text: Venues where one's tried making dates, with space limited

indicators.note: limited here means hemmed in: the courting word closes round the space word

parts.note: courts means woos or goes out with someone
room means space

explanation.surface: Someone goes courting in a cramped place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's tried' suggests trying something on; it means being put on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Trials are held in law courts, so these chambers are where a defendant is tried.

clue.text: One has a share in the lead in Central American country, losing 33 per cent

definitions.text: One has a share in the lead

indicators.note: losing means the country's name sheds some of its letters

parts.note: Costa Rica is a country in Central America
a third of the nine-letter name, its final three letters

explanation.surface: A shareholder in a Central American nation's economy loses a third of their stake.
explanation.walkthrough: COSTA RICA has nine letters; 'losing 33 per cent' drops three, ICA.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star shares top billing, the leading role, with another actor.

clue.text: Out-of-control gunner guilty — nothing odd about that

indicators.note: no odd letters are kept, so only the even-placed letters of the two words remain

explanation.surface: A soldier found guilty of indiscipline, and nobody thinks it strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing odd about that' keeps the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of gunner and guilty: U N R, U L Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An unruly crowd or child is disorderly and beyond control, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Single-minded concentration that Tube driver needs?

definitions.meaning: a narrow focus on one goal, ignoring everything else
a London Underground driver literally has to look along the tunnel ahead

explanation.surface: An Underground train driver must stay focused.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway, which runs through tunnels.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a blinkered fixation on one aim to the exclusion of all else.

clue.text: Paddles topless and bottomless — rude!

indicators.note: without its top and bottom, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: coarse means rude or vulgar

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at people paddling with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless and bottomless' strips C and E from COARSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars are the blades used to row or paddle a boat, so a noun synonym.

clue.text: Like a protestor, agitated, lit many houses alight!

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other
agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: lit means alight, burning

explanation.surface: An agitated protestor sets many houses on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges LIT MANY into MIANTLY, and 'houses' puts LIT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestor acts aggressively in support of a cause, which is acting in a combative, activist manner.

clue.text: Wager placed by a very old character

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A bet laid by an elderly eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter here: beta is the second letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, which dates from antiquity, hence a very old written symbol.

clue.text: Keep watch on ship — it's a cosmetic thing

parts.note: to eye something is to keep watch on it
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on a ship and remarks on its glamour.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up drawn along the lid, a type of cosmetic.

clue.text: Metal arm is taut inside, having over-reactive nerves

indicators.note: inside says the letters lie within the run of words that precedes it

explanation.surface: A tense metal arm, like someone's jumpy nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' points to metAL ARM IST aut.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist panics too easily, raising fears out of proportion to the danger.

clue.text: Food things carried out by tumbler

definitions.meaning: a Chinese starter of filled, fried pastry
an acrobat performs a spring and a roll

explanation.surface: Snacks produced by a drinking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbler' looks like a glass; it is an acrobat, whose moves include springs and rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crisp fried pastry roll of Chinese cuisine, an item eaten as a starter.

clue.text: Greek grub takes fine time to arrive?

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
ETA, estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: Greek food arrives fine, but late.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white cheese from Greece, a national foodstuff.

clue.text: Say kite's electronic rival gets snagged in tree — perfect picture!

parts.note: a kite is an example of a bird, here possessive

indicators.note: caught up inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a yew is a tree
vie means compete, rival

explanation.surface: A kite and a drone tangle in a tree, giving a great photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks kite as just one example of a bird; 'electronic rival' looks like a drone but gives two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from overhead gives a complete overall picture of the scene below.

clue.text: Having a night out?

parts.note: 'out' means unconscious, spending the night out cold in bed rather than out partying

explanation.surface: A question about going out on the town.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping is dead to the world through the night, out like a light.

clue.text: Acceptance I should split costs — I'm bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to splitting the costs because they are broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' signals the rearrangement; 'should split' only knits the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoicism is patient endurance of hardship, a calm resignation to what comes.

clue.text: These days, initially, this could be commercial

definitions.meaning: the current era, years counted from Christ's birth
its initials, AD, also stand for an advert

explanation.surface: Nowadays, it all starts as advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase labels the present era of dates, the years of our Lord.

clue.text: Party costume outfit for ironing?

definitions.meaning: clothing for smoothing out, making things even

explanation.surface: Clothes worn while doing the ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is formal wear such as a gown or dinner jacket worn to an evening function.

clue.text: Scraps in short sleeves, perhaps, cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the last letter round to the front

parts.note: short sleeves have no cuffs, so one is cuffless

explanation.surface: Fights break out among cyclists in T-shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' brings the final S of CUFFLESS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps and scuffles are both brief, untidy fights.

clue.text: Small ode — 'In a state / Slid, not straight'

indicators.note: in a state means agitated, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A little poem about a state, with a couplet on sliding crookedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier who slaloms zigzags between gates rather than going straight downhill.

clue.text: Grouped in 'Archaic/Old' — should e-readers disregard?

indicators.note: grouped in says the letters are gathered within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Should readers of e-books ignore a section labelled old-fashioned?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouped in' points to archaiC/OLD SHOULD E-Readers.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the brush-off is to snub and deliberately ignore them.

clue.text: Mental block getting ring off?

explanation.surface: A psychological problem about phone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means both an inhibition and putting the phone down.

clue.text: Mr Chi Minh walked, speedy thing

parts.note: Ho Chi Minh, the Vietnamese leader, so Mr Ho
trod means walked

explanation.surface: The Vietnamese leader walked, which was quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot rod is a car modified for high speed and acceleration.

clue.text: Support cricket side being put in again

parts.note: to follow a team is to support it
the on side is the leg side of a cricket pitch

explanation.surface: A cricket fan backs a team sent in to bat again.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a side well behind may be made to bat ('put in') again straight away: that is the follow-on.
explanation.definitionFit: The follow-on is a cricket team being sent in to bat a second time immediately.

clue.text: Four-foot boat?

parts.note: not a tiny craft but one powered by the feet of two people on pedals

explanation.surface: A query about a boat four feet long.
explanation.walkthrough: A pedalo is a small pleasure boat driven by pedals, common at British seaside resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The craft is propelled by two riders pedalling, so four feet drive it.

clue.text: One walks in this small garden

parts.note: to garden can mean to hoe

explanation.surface: A tiny garden for a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is what a person walks in.

clue.text: I'm a farm animal and am kept in pound

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A farm animal talks about being penned.
explanation.walkthrough: A pound is also an animal pen, which makes 'kept in pound' read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A young sheep is a familiar livestock creature on farms.

clue.text: One's tasty if fresh, with gin in a cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A drink is tasty if made with fresh gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a cocktail' mixes IF FRESH and GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded cod sticks are a popular and tasty British food.

clue.text: In Spain so long, but no one knocked back drink

indicators.note: knocked back means turned back, so the word is read in reverse
no one means without the numeral-like letter for one

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A goodbye in Spain over a drink that nobody downed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no one' removes I from ADIOS, leaving ADOS; 'knocked back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink or mixer.

clue.text: Bashed in passing drunk despised around women's group

indicators.note: around says the scrambled word surrounds the other piece
drunk means unsteady, so the letters are reeled into a new order

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute

explanation.surface: A drunk lashes out at a women's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives SIDESPED, the anagram of DESPISED. The WI, Women's Institute, is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: To sideswipe is to strike glancingly while going past.
